# Was the Roll20 data breach a hack?

**Confirmed.** Yes, by Roll20's own account: an unauthorized third party got into its system on Nov 16 and reached account records. Who did it is not known.

Incident: Roll20 account data breach, Nov 2026. Also reported as the Roll20 hack and the Roll20 security incident. First published Nov 20, 2026; last updated Nov 20, 2026, 11:46 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Roll20, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 20, 2026, 11:46 PM ET: **Roll20 says an outsider reached account records for under 1% of users on Nov 16, including password hashes.** First draft. 2 sources (1 Tier 1), 17 claims (10 Confirmed, 2 Reported, 5 Not established), 7 questions. Roll20's forum notice confirms the intrusion; the upload-flaw detail is from its email via one outlet. No attacker named. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Local. Roll20 says fewer than 1% of its users were affected. It claims over 15 million players, so that is up to about 150,000 accounts on one gaming site, worldwide.
- Who is affected: Roll20 users who got the company's warning email. Their names, emails and password hashes were involved, and for some the last 4 digits of a saved card.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| <1% | Users affected | Roll20's figure; no count given |
| Nov 16 | Access found and blocked | Evening, per Roll20 |
| Last 4 | Card digits, for some | No full card numbers |

### Known so far

- An unauthorized third party got into Roll20's system on the evening of Nov 16; Roll20 blocked the access.
- Fewer than 1% of Roll20 users were affected, and each was emailed.
- Names, email addresses and salted bcrypt password hashes were involved.
- Some users with a saved card had the last 4 digits involved; full card numbers were not.

### Not known yet

- Who was behind it.
- How many accounts, as a number.
- Whether any data was copied. Roll20 says it found no evidence of it.
- Why Roll20 believes the attack was AI-assisted.
- Which software had the flaw.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of 11:45 PM ET on Nov 20, 2026.

- Coverage by an established news outlet. One outlet, Privacy Affairs, has reported it; sites that summarise that report are not counted.
- The text of Roll20's email on a Roll20 page. We have its wording only as Privacy Affairs quotes it.
- The number of affected accounts.
- Which software had the upload flaw.
- Any evidence for Roll20's belief that the attack was AI-assisted.
- A claim of responsibility, or any attacker named.
- Word on whether DriveThruRPG or other services Roll20 runs were touched.
